english_translation: Go together, speak together, let your minds come to a common understanding, as the gods of old, in accord, attend upon their allotted share.
context_summary: The hymn’s voice addresses an assembly in the plural. It holds up the gods gathering around their allotted share as a pattern for human agreement.
derived_principle: Record the constraints each party must meet. Test the options against the constraints they accept in common.

iast_transliteration: akṣairmā dīvyaḥ kṛṣimitkṛṣasva vitte ramasva bahu manyamānaḥ | tatra gāvaḥ kitava tatra jāyā tanme vi caṣṭe savitāyamaryaḥ ||
english_translation: Do not play at dice. Work the soil instead and delight in what you possess, valuing it highly. There are your cattle, gambler, and there your wife. Thus has this noble Savitṛ instructed me.
context_summary: After the gambler’s account of longing and household distress, the voice addresses a dice player directly. The counsel to return to cultivation is attributed to Savitṛ.

sanskrit_devanagari: यस्तु सर्वाणि भूतान्यात्मन्नेवानुपश्यति । सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं ततो न वि चिकित्सति ॥

english_translation: But one who sees all beings in the Self alone, and the Self in all beings, thereafter has no doubt.

derived_principle: Before choosing for others, identify one assumption about their experience and test it with the people affected.

english_translation: Whatever an eminent person does, other people do likewise. Whatever standard that person establishes, the world follows.

derived_principle: Before taking a visible shortcut, ask what would happen if everyone copied it. Demonstrate the practice you expect others to repeat.

english_translation: Kingship can be accomplished with helpers. A single wheel does not turn. Therefore the king should appoint advisers and hear their judgment.

derived_principle: Before committing others to a plan, obtain evidence from the people who know its dependencies and record what changed.

sanskrit_devanagari: सर्वमात्ययिकं कार्यं शृणुयान्नातिपातयेत् । कृच्छ्रसाध्यमतिक्रान्तमसाध्यं वापि जायते ॥

english_translation: May we hear what is auspicious with our ears, O gods. May we see what is auspicious with our eyes, O ones worthy of worship. Praising you with steady limbs and bodies, may we live out the span of life allotted by the gods.
context_summary: A group of worshippers addresses the gods together, asking for sound perception, bodily steadiness and the full course of life. The image of steady limbs belongs to a prayer of praise.
derived_principle: When noise or alarm makes observation unreliable, take a brief, bounded pause and obtain one independently checkable observation.

edition: The Upanishads in the Light of Sri Aurobindo, Sanskrit text. English is an editorial translation.
sanskrit_devanagari:
अन्यच्छ्रेयोऽन्यदुतैव प्रेयस्ते उभे नानार्थे पुरुषँ सिनीतः । तयोः श्रेय आददानस्य साधु भवति हीयतेऽर्थाद्य उ प्रेयो वृणीते ॥
श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतः तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीरः । श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभि प्रेयसो वृणीते प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद्वृणीते ॥
iast_transliteration:
anyacchreyo’nyadutaiva preyaste ubhe nānārthe puruṣam̐ sinītaḥ | tayoḥ śreya ādadānasya sādhu bhavati hīyate’rthādya u preyo vṛṇīte ||
śreyaśca preyaśca manuṣyametaḥ tau samparītya vivinakti dhīraḥ | śreyo hi dhīro’bhi preyaso vṛṇīte preyo mando yogakṣemādvṛṇīte ||
english_translation:
The good is one thing, the pleasant another. These two bind a person to different ends. It goes well for one who takes up the good. Whoever chooses the pleasant falls away from the goal.
The good and the pleasant both approach a person. Having examined them, the discerning person distinguishes them and chooses the good over the pleasant. The dull person chooses the pleasant for the sake of acquiring and keeping what they have.
context_summary: Yama addresses Naciketas after the boy has declined attractive gifts in place of knowledge about death. Yama distinguishes two ends a chooser may pursue, even when both options are appealing.
derived_principle: Before an exclusive commitment, state the end each option serves and which opportunity accepting it permanently forfeits.

edition: The Upanishads in the Light of Sri Aurobindo, Sanskrit text. English is an editorial translation.
sanskrit_devanagari:
त्रयाः प्राजापत्याः प्रजापतौ पितरि ब्रह्मचर्यम् ऊषुः । देवा मनुष्या असुराः । उषित्वा ब्रह्मचर्यं देवा ऊचुर् ब्रवीतु नो भवान् इति । तेभ्यो हैतद् अक्षरम् उवाच द इति । व्यज्ञासिष्टा३ इति । व्यज्ञासिष्मेति होचुः । दाम्यतेति न आत्थेति । ओम् इति होवाच व्यज्ञासिष्टेति ॥
अथ हैनं मनुष्या ऊचुर् ब्रवीतु नो भवान् इति । तेभ्यो हैतद् एवाक्षरम् उवाच द इति । व्यज्ञासिष्टा३ इति । व्यज्ञासिष्मेति होचुः । दत्तेति न आत्थेति । ओम् इति होवाच व्यज्ञासिष्टेति ॥
अथ हैनम् असुरा ऊचुर् ब्रवीतु नो भवान् इति । तेभ्यो हैतद् एवाक्षरम् उवाच द इति । व्यज्ञासिष्टा३ इति । व्यज्ञासिष्मेति होचुः । दयध्वम् इति न आत्थेति । ओम् इति होवाच व्यज्ञासिष्टेति । तद् एतद् एवैषा दैवी वाग् अनुवदति स्तनयित्नुर् द द द इति । दम्यत दत्त दयध्वम् इति । तद् एतत् त्रयं शिक्षेद् दमम् दानम् दयाम् इति ॥
iast_transliteration:
trayāḥ prājāpatyāḥ prajāpatau pitari brahmacaryam ūṣuḥ | devā manuṣyā asurāḥ | uṣitvā brahmacaryaṃ devā ūcur bravītu no bhavān iti | tebhyo haitad akṣaram uvāca da iti | vyajñāsiṣṭā3 iti | vyajñāsiṣmeti hocuḥ | dāmyateti na āttheti | om iti hovāca vyajñāsiṣṭeti ||
atha hainaṃ manuṣyā ūcur bravītu no bhavān iti | tebhyo haitad evākṣaram uvāca da iti | vyajñāsiṣṭā3 iti | vyajñāsiṣmeti hocuḥ | datteti na āttheti | om iti hovāca vyajñāsiṣṭeti ||
atha hainam asurā ūcur bravītu no bhavān iti | tebhyo haitad evākṣaram uvāca da iti | vyajñāsiṣṭā3 iti | vyajñāsiṣmeti hocuḥ | dayadhvam iti na āttheti | om iti hovāca vyajñāsiṣṭeti | tad etad evaiṣā daivī vāg anuvadati stanayitnur da da da iti | damyata datta dayadhvam iti | tad etat trayaṃ śikṣed damam dānam dayām iti ||
english_translation:
Three kinds of offspring of Prajāpati lived as students with their father Prajāpati: gods, humans and asuras. Having completed their studentship, the gods said, ‘Please instruct us, sir.’ He spoke the syllable da to them and asked, ‘Did you understand?’ ‘We understood,’ they said. ‘You told us to restrain ourselves.’ ‘Yes,’ he said, ‘you understood.’
Then the humans said to him, ‘Please instruct us, sir.’ He spoke that same syllable da to them and asked, ‘Did you understand?’ ‘We understood,’ they said. ‘You told us to give.’ ‘Yes,’ he said, ‘you understood.’
Then the asuras said to him, ‘Please instruct us, sir.’ He spoke that same syllable da to them and asked, ‘Did you understand?’ ‘We understood,’ they said. ‘You told us to show compassion.’ ‘Yes,’ he said, ‘you understood.’ This very instruction the divine voice of thunder repeats as da, da, da: restrain yourselves, give, show compassion. One should learn these three: restraint, generosity and compassion.
context_summary: Prajāpati’s three groups of children ask their father for instruction. Each hears the same syllable through a different imperative, and the narrator closes by asking the learner to cultivate all three.
derived_principle: Identify the behavior producing the shortfall. Restrain overreach, release resources that are being withheld, or relieve a burden imposed on someone else.

edition: The Upanishads in the Light of Sri Aurobindo, Sanskrit text. English is an editorial translation.
sanskrit_devanagari: सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः । येनाक्रमन्त्यृषयो ह्याप्तकामा यत्र तत्सत्यस्य परमं निधानम् ॥
iast_transliteration: satyameva jayate nānṛtaṃ satyena panthā vitato devayānaḥ | yenākramantyṛṣayo hyāptakāmā yatra tatsatyasya paramaṃ nidhānam ||
english_translation: Truth alone prevails, never falsehood. By truth the path of the gods is laid out, along which the seers whose desires have been fulfilled ascend to where truth has its highest abode.
context_summary: In Aṅgiras’s teaching to Śaunaka, truth belongs to the discipline through which the Self is reached. The verse links truth to the seers’ path and its highest destination.
derived_principle: Before putting a consequential statement on the permanent record, distinguish what the evidence establishes, what remains uncertain and who needs to receive it.
scenarios_json: [{"scenario":"A lab director must certify an archived result today and discovers that two observations in the draft never occurred.","suggested_solution":"Check the original logs, strike the unsupported observations and submit the signed correction with an audit trail to the authorized recipient."},{"scenario":"During a recorded awards ceremony a presenter discovers the announced winner was calculated using a duplicated ballot.","suggested_solution":"Pause the announcement, verify the tally with the counter, and give the corrected result on record, preserving the reason for the change."}]

application_limit: Once a verified disclosure reaches its audience it cannot be unheard. Truthfulness alone does not settle confidentiality, audience or the proper reporting route. Sattvic is an editorial target-state label.

edition: The Upanishads in the Light of Sri Aurobindo, Sanskrit text. English is an editorial translation.
sanskrit_devanagari: ईशा वास्यमिदं सर्वं यत् किञ्च जगत्यां जगत् । तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथा मा गृधः कस्यस्विद् धनम् ॥
iast_transliteration: īśā vāsyamidaṃ sarvaṃ yat kiñca jagatyāṃ jagat | tena tyaktena bhuñjīthā mā gṛdhaḥ kasyasvid dhanam ||
english_translation: All this, whatever moves in this moving world, is to be clothed in the Lord. Enjoy through that relinquishment. Do not covet anyone’s wealth.
context_summary: The opening mantra addresses the hearer about the world, its relation to the Lord and the use of possessions. The injunction against coveting follows the compact expression about enjoyment through relinquishment.
derived_principle: Before consuming a nonrenewable stock, establish who has a claim, what minimum use meets the purpose, and who can authorize that use.
scenarios_json: [{"scenario":"A lab has one remaining sample from a discontinued collection. Use a reversible mock-up to verify that both keepsakes fit."}]
misapplication_scenario: A trustee invokes renunciation to withhold supplies from the people the stock was collected to serve.

edition: Sanskrit Documents, Dhruvasūktam, RV 10.173. English is an editorial translation. Vedic pitch accents are omitted.
sanskrit_devanagari:
आ त्वाहार्षमन्तरेधि ध्रुवस्तिष्ठाविचाचलिः । विशस्त्वा सर्वा वाञ्छन्तु मा त्वद्राष्ट्रमधि भ्रशत् ॥
इहैवैधि माप च्योष्ठाः पर्वत इवाविचाचलिः । इन्द्र इवेह ध्रुवस्तिष्ठेह राष्ट्रमु धारय ॥
iast_transliteration:
ā tvāhārṣamantaredhi dhruvastiṣṭhāvicācaliḥ | viśastvā sarvā vāñchantu mā tvadrāṣṭramadhi bhraśat ||
ihaivaidhi māpa cyoṣṭhāḥ parvata ivāvicācaliḥ | indra iveha dhruvastiṣṭheha rāṣṭramu dhāraya ||
english_translation:
I have brought you here. Be among us. Stand firm, unwavering. May all the clans desire you, and may the realm not slip away from you.
Remain right here. Do not fall away. Be unwavering like a mountain. Stand firm here like Indra, and uphold the realm here.
context_summary: A ritual speaker addresses a ruler being established in office. The wish for acceptance among the clans accompanies a charge to remain firm and sustain the realm.
derived_principle: Maintain a publicly stated service commitment through a change of leadership. Ask those who rely on it how they will detect a lapse.
scenarios_json: [{"scenario":"A new library director inherits a promise to open on evenings during exams, but the rota disappeared in the handover.","suggested_solution":"Confirm the dates with users, publish a staffed rota and designate a deputy empowered to fill gaps."},{"scenario":"A youth club elects a new coordinator midway through a season while several families depend on the published pickup schedule.","suggested_solution":"Reconfirm the schedule with families and name a contact who can resolve missed pickups throughout the transition."}]
misapplication_scenario: An incumbent cites steadfastness to disregard a valid vote ending their mandate.
application_limit: This is a royal installation hymn. Review, succession and public accountability are contemporary applications. Continued authority needs its own basis. Sattvic is an editorial target-state label.

edition: Vedshala, Śaunaka Atharvaveda, Bhūmi Sūkta. English is an editorial translation. Vedic pitch accents are omitted.
sanskrit_devanagari: जनं बिभ्रती बहुधा विवाचसं नानाधर्माणं पृथिवी यथौकसम् । सहस्रं धारा द्रविणस्य मे दुहां ध्रुवेव धेनुरनपस्फुरन्ती ॥
iast_transliteration: janaṃ bibhratī bahudhā vivācasaṃ nānādharmāṇaṃ pṛthivī yathaukasam | sahasraṃ dhārā draviṇasya me duhāṃ dhruveva dhenuranapasphurantī ||
english_translation: May Earth, bearing people of many different languages and varied observances, each in their own dwelling, yield me a thousand streams of wealth like a steady cow that does not kick away.
context_summary: The speaker of the Earth hymn describes the different peoples Earth sustains and asks her for abundance. Their differences of speech and observance coexist in the image of a common source of support.
derived_principle: When groups share a scarce service, compare actual access by language and custom, then test a common rule with accommodations.
scenarios_json: [{"scenario":"A reservation platform serves three language groups, but its cancellation terms exist in only one language.","suggested_solution":"Translate and user-test the terms, retain the same cancellation window and compare missed refunds by language after launch."},{"scenario":"Two community groups cannot use the hall during different observances and compete for the same remaining evenings.","suggested_solution":"Collect the blocked dates privately, publish a rotation and review whether either group repeatedly loses usable slots."}]
misapplication_scenario: An organizer assumes that everyone who speaks a particular language observes the same dates and excludes them from booking.
application_limit: The hymn gives an image of plurality and abundance. It supplies no quota or evidence of any individual’s needs. Sattvic is an editorial target-state label.

edition: Bhagavad Gita, The Song of God, Sanskrit text accompanying Swami Mukundananda. English is an editorial translation.
sanskrit_devanagari: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः पृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसम्मूढचेताः । यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मे शिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥
iast_transliteration: kārpaṇyadoṣopahatasvabhāvaḥ pṛcchāmi tvāṃ dharmasammūḍhacetāḥ | yacchreyaḥ syānniścitaṃ brūhi tanme śiṣyaste’haṃ śādhi māṃ tvāṃ prapannam ||
english_translation: My natural disposition is overcome by the fault of faintheartedness, and my mind is bewildered about duty. I ask you to tell me decisively what would be better. I am your pupil. Instruct me, who have sought refuge in you.
context_summary: Arjuna speaks to Krishna after setting out his conflicting loyalties and his uncertainty over what action is right. He changes the terms of the conversation by explicitly asking to be taught.
derived_principle: When your loyalties make it hard to weigh evidence, name the conflict and ask a qualified, disinterested person to examine the options.

edition: Bhagavad Gita, The Song of God, Sanskrit text accompanying Swami Mukundananda. English is an editorial translation.
sanskrit_devanagari: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः । आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ॥
iast_transliteration: mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ | āgamāpāyino’nityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata ||
english_translation: Contacts of the senses, son of Kuntī, give rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and do not endure. Bear with them, descendant of Bharata.
context_summary: Krishna addresses Arjuna in the early teaching about what endures through bodily change. Alternating sensations supply the immediate example of an experience that passes.
derived_principle: When a disturbance fits a known transient pattern, retain the plan until a stated review time. Define evidence that would trigger earlier intervention.

application_limit: The verse concerns sensory experience. Whether an external process is transient must be tested against current evidence. Sattvic is an editorial target-state label.

english_translation: Satyakāma Jābāla asked his mother Jabālā, “I wish to live as a student. What is my lineage?” She said, “My child, I do not know your lineage. I had you in my youth while moving about in service. I do not know your lineage. I am Jabālā and you are Satyakāma. Call yourself Satyakāma Jābāla.” He approached Hāridrumata Gautama: “Sir, I wish to live with you as a student. May I come to you?” Asked his lineage, he replied, “Sir, I do not know. I asked my mother. She told me she had me while moving about in service in her youth and does not know my lineage. She is Jabālā and I am Satyakāma. Thus I am Satyakāma Jābāla, sir.” Gautama said, “Only a Brahmin could speak thus. Bring fuel, dear boy. I will initiate you, for you have held to the truth.” Having initiated him, he separated four hundred thin, weak cows and told him to follow them. Driving them out, Satyakāma said, “I will return only with a thousand.” He stayed away for years, until they numbered a thousand.
